requirements_summary: Workload types: chat-like assistant + doc search embeddings for retrieval augmentation.

Concurrency: typical concurrent requests 10-20; expected peak concurrency ~60-80 during bursts.
Error tolerance: zero 429s during live demos; acceptable to surface 429s in background tasks with auto-retry.
Cost sensitivity: high — looks for Optimize recommendations (batching, caching, token controls).
Model preferences: small/medium open models for most flows; fallback to larger model for customer-facing demo outputs.

technical_notes: They currently use a serverless architecture on AWS (API Gateway + Lambda + Redis for sessions).
Concern: cold-start amplification causing bursts of concurrent calls from lambda fleet — want guidance on connection reuse and pooling.
SE suggestion: use connection pooling, client-side request queueing with concurrency cap, and short exponential backoff with full jitter.
Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions: intelligent batching and prefix caching to reduce per-token spend during spikes.
